# Kurviq

> Kurviq (https://kurviq.com) is a free online whiteboard built on Excalidraw (unofficial), with named scenes, slides and formatted text. No account: drawings live in the user's browser and can optionally be synced with a GitHub repository. AI agents draw and edit with the user through a remote MCP server that works via the user's open Kurviq tab.

## Connect an agent (MCP)

1. Add `https://kurviq.com/mcp` as a remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth sign-in):
   - Claude Code: `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http kurviq https://kurviq.com/mcp` (all projects), then `/mcp` → kurviq → Authenticate
   - Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`): `[mcp_servers.kurviq]` with `url = "https://kurviq.com/mcp"`, then `codex mcp login kurviq`
   - Claude Desktop / claude.ai: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → the URL
   - Cursor and others: `{"mcpServers": {"kurviq": {"url": "https://kurviq.com/mcp"}}}`
2. On first use the MCP client opens the user's browser: a Kurviq page asks the user to allow the agent. It must be the browser the user works in Kurviq with (the page reads that browser's agent access). The client keeps the tokens and renews them by itself.
3. The tools work while Kurviq is open in that browser (any scene, any tab). If a tool answers "Kurviq is not open", ask the user to open https://kurviq.com and try again.

The address holds no secret. The user signs out every agent at once in Kurviq (MCP → "Sign out all agents"). The old personal link `https://kurviq.com/mcp/<key>` doesn't work any more: sign in with `https://kurviq.com/mcp`.

## How to work with the user's drawings

The MCP server's instructions (sent on connect) explain everything in detail. In short:

- Call `read_me` once: the element format (shapes, labels, arrows with bindings, images, formatted text, slides).
- New drawing: `create_view` (draft, the user may see it live in their client) → `save_scene(name, checkpointId)`.
- Change an existing scene: always `read_scene(name)` first, then `edit_scene(name, basedOn: revision, add / update / delete)`. Edit only the elements you mean; never re-create a scene the user works on. `edit_scene` returns an image of the result.
- `read_scene(name, since: revision)` reports exactly what the user changed by hand since your last edit (`userChanges`).
- `view_scene` returns a real PNG (rendered in the user's tab with Excalidraw itself). `measure_text` measures text with the real fonts.
- Slides: every frame is a slide; a "Template" frame holds header/footer/logo. `validate_deck` checks a deck (text that doesn't fit, cut-off elements, contrast, …).
- Formatted text: write markdown in `text` (bold, italic, lists, checklists, links, sizes).
- Images and icons: `{ "type": "image", "src": "<http(s) or data URL>" }`, `"svg": "<svg…>"` or `"icon": "lucide:database"`.
- `app_status`: which scene the user has open, whether GitHub is connected (`github`), each scene's sync status. `open_scene` switches what the user sees: only when they ask.
- Don't push, write files or call HTTP APIs yourself: the tools and the user's app do all syncing and merging.

## GitHub (optional, per browser)

- Without GitHub every scene is local-only: it exists only in that browser. Agents read and edit local-only scenes the same way.
- With GitHub (Connect GitHub → allow the Kurviq GitHub App), scenes are stored as `scenes/<name>.excalidraw` in the user's private repository `<account>/kurviq-scenes` (Kurviq creates it). Edits are pushed about 10 s after the user stops drawing; other people's changes arrive within a minute and are merged element by element. Agent edits are commits by the user's GitHub account, marked with a `Scenes-Source: agent` trailer.
- Teams: a space is a GitHub account or organization with its `<owner>/kurviq-scenes`; the user switches spaces in the Scenes sidebar, and the tools work on the open space. Permissions are GitHub's: with read access only, `app_status` reports `github: read only …` and edits are refused.
- Fonts: besides Excalidraw's own, any Google font works by its exact name, e.g. `"fontFamily": "Inter"` (fetched on first use, then carried by the scene); `add_font("Inter")` adds one ahead. `app_status` lists added fonts as `customFonts`. Font files are added by the user (font picker → "Add font…").
- Sharing: scenes have links `https://kurviq.com/@<owner>/<scene>`. Public scenes (in `<owner>/kurviq-public`) open for everyone; private ones for people who can read the repository on GitHub. The raw JSON of a public scene: `https://kurviq.com/api/public/<owner>/<scene>`. Add `?present` (and `&slide=3`) to a scene link to open it presenting.
- The connection stays for months: Kurviq keeps a refresh token in an encrypted, httpOnly cookie of the browser (nothing is stored on Kurviq's server). Disconnect any time in the Scenes sidebar.

## Limits of the online version

- Local file paths (image `src`, edit files) don't work: Kurviq's MCP server runs on kurviq.com, not on the agent's machine. Images from your machine: upload them with `curl -s --data-binary @image.png <upload address>` (the upload address is in the MCP server's instructions and tool descriptions, valid for a week; PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG up to 10 MB), then add `{ "type": "image", "fileId": "<the answer's fileId>", "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 800 }`. The image's bytes never pass through your context; it goes straight to the user's open Kurviq tab.
- `export_pdf` is not available through MCP; the user exports PDFs in Kurviq (Slides sidebar → PDF).
- Want everything on your own machine (local Excalidraw, git CLI, headless rendering without an open tab)? Use the local install: https://github.com/tecsteps/kurviq

## Links
